 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant-petitioner challenging the judgment and award dated 24.01.2019 passed in MVC.No.1019/2014 by the learned I Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Member,
MACT Kalaburagi (for short 'the Tribunal').
2.
Though this appeal is listed for admission, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the tribunal has committed a gross error in not considering any material evidence both oral and documentary and has awarded meager and inadequate compensation, which requires to be enhanced.
Further it is submitted that the notional income is on the lower side.
He further submits that the tribunal has held that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.
Hence, on these grounds sought for enhancement of compensation and prays to allow the appeal.

To substantiate his arguments, he relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pappu and Others Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another in Civil Appeal No.20962/2017 dated 19.01.2018 wherein the pay and recover is applicable.

entities.text: Pappu and Others Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent- Insurance Company supports the judgment and award of the Tribunal and therefore contended that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal be not disturbed so also the liability of the Insurance Company.
Further submits that the petitioner is the sole dependant of the deceased, hence 50% to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
Hence, prays to dismiss the appeal.

To substantiate her arguments, she relied on the judgments of this Court in MFA No.20759/2012 C/w MFA No.24357/2011 dated 15.04.2019 and MFA No.200225/2015 C/w MFA No.200628/2015.
6. Having heard the arguments of the learned counsel for both parties and on perusal of records the following points would arise for consideration:
(1) Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?
(2) Whether the Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation under the principle of "pay and recover"?

2
(3) What order/award?

7. My answer to the above points are:
(1) Partly affirmative (2) Affirmative.
(3) As per final order 8.
Insofar as quantum of compensation is concerned, the deceased was aged 59 years as on the date of the accident.
It is contended that the deceased was doing agriculture work and running grocery shop and getting monthly Rs.15,000/- p.m.
In support of the contention, the petitioner has not tendered any evidence.
In the absence of any evidence or proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed as per the Lokadalat chart issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has taken place in the year 2014, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.7,500/- p.m. as per chart.

In view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, to the aforesaid amount, 10% has to be added on account of future prospects as the deceased was aged about 59 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.8,250/-.
9.

I have perused the judgment of the Co-ordinate bench of the Court in MFA No.20759/2012 C/w MFA NO.24357/2011 dated 15.04.2019, wherein this Court has deducted 50% of the income towards personal expenses of the deceased as the petitioner is one wife and other is petitioner is major son.

In the case on hand, a perusal of the decision of Sarla Verma's case their lordship's have held that where the deceased was married the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be 1/3rd.
Hence, relying on the said decision, the tribunal has rightly deducted 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
Hence, in this regard, the arguments put-forth by the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-Insurance Company cannot be accepted.

Therefore,
the petitioner for compensation under the head loss of dependency of Rs.5,94,000/- (Rs.5,550 x 12 x 9) as against Rs.5,54,364/- awarded by the Tribunal.

10. In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of N. Jayashree and Others Vs. Cholamandalam Ms. General Insurance Company Ltd. reported in AIR 2021 SC 5218, the petitioner is also entitled for compensation towards loss of consortium.

entities.text: N. Jayashree and Others Vs. Cholamandalam Ms. General Insurance Company Ltd. reported in AIR 2021 SC 5218
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, I answer point No.1 partly affirmative.

11. In view of the above discussions, the petitioner would be entitled for enhancement of compensation as mentioned in the table below:
 As awarded by As awarded  Head the Tribunal by this Court  (Rs.) (Rs.)
Loss of dependency and loss of 5,54,364 5,94,000/-
future income Towards love and affection 30,000/- -----
Towards loss of consortium 40,000/- 44,000/-
loss of estate and funeral 30,000/- 33,000/-
Smt.Shivamma W/O Late Sidramappa vs Mallikarjun And Ors on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92885363/
3 expenses

With regard to liability of the Insurance Company is concerned, the tribunal has dismissed the claim petition as against respondent Nos.1 and 3 on the ground that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.

However, in view of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pappu's case stated supra, the respondent-Insurance Company cannot escape from its liability and shall satisfy the award amount with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, I answer point No.2 in the affirmative.

13. For the aforesaid reasons and discussions, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER (a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The judgment and award passed by the tribunal is modified.

(c) The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,71,000/- as against Rs.6,54,400/-
awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at 6% interest from the date of petition till realization.
(d) The respondent Nos.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

(e) The respondent-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
(f) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.
(g) Draw award accordingly.
